shared_elements: upright rectangular stone slab/pillar with flat carved face
low-relief carved animal shown in profile
quadruped with elongated body and tail
plain undecorated ground surrounding the relief (in A) / partly plain lower field (in B)
weathered stone set in an excavated rubble-and-earth setting
justification: Both are upright flat-faced stone slabs bearing shallow, rounded low-relief carving whose most specific correspondence is an elongated quadruped in strict profile with a long tail rendered as a raised silhouette against a plain ground. The decisive difference is density and organisation: A carries a single isolated animal on a largely empty field, while B is a crowded, register-based composition with a row of arched motifs, a band of vertical hatching, and several animal and figural elements stacked in horizontal tiers.
